html:
Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni is a town in western French Guiana, on the Maroni River facing Suriname. It was founded in 1858 as the centre of the French penal colony, and for decades was run by the prison administration.

Every convict shipped from France landed at its Camp de la Transportation, where prisoners were sorted and sent to camps in the forest or to the islands off the coast, including Devil's Island. Convicts built the town's streets, houses and hospital. Freed convicts were often forced to stay in the colony for years, living in poverty. The writer Henri Charrière, author of Papillon, passed through it.

The penal colony closed after 1946, and the last prisoners left in 1953. The camp is now a museum. The town has grown fast through migration from Suriname and the river, and is the second town of French Guiana.
